title: Ledger Coding Reference — No-Show Fees Inside the Documentation Window on Pre-Placement Statements
content:
**Entry: no-show fee pending documentation.** The most recently posted no-show fee on the Patient Financial Account, whose open part is its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it, is left off the pre-placement statement while its missed visit is inside the documentation window of the visit's type — that is, while the handling date is no more than the waiver documentation days that In-Person Appointments sets for that visit type, counted in calendar days after the visit date:

| Missed visit inside its documentation window | The visit type waives a first no-show under In-Person Appointments | Left off the pre-placement statement |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the fee's whole open part |
| yes | no | 50 percent of the fee's open part |
| no — the window has closed | either | nothing; the fee is shown |

**How the records are read.**

- The fee is the no-show fee charge posted last on the account; its encounter number identifies the In-Person Appointments record of the missed visit, and that record's visit type gives the documentation window and whether a first no-show is waived.
- The visit date is the date of service carried on the no-show fee charge.
- A fee with no open part left leaves nothing off.

**Hypothetical cases.** A no-show fee of 60.00 with nothing paid against it, for a visit type with a (hypothetical) 14-day documentation window that does not waive a first no-show: on a handling date 10 days after the visit, 30.00 is left off; on a handling date 14 days after the visit, 30.00 is still left off; on a handling date 15 days after, nothing is left off. Had the visit type waived a first no-show, 60.00 would be left off on days 10 and 14.
